title: Incident-lane closure: control-domain reviews and three-witness certificates
summary: Methodology 10.39 enables incident-lane closure for five reviewed CCIP pilot lanes only: FRNT on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base and Optimism, and yUSD on Ethereum. Closure begins only after the first post-deploy screening cycle writes admitted v2 certificates and matching current issuer/provider reviews exist. A missing certificate closes nothing. The derived join binds the exact lane, contributors, emitter runtime pins and event families to the frozen screening policy and the descriptor's own contiguous chain. Verifier-compromise exposure requires valid point-in-time exemption evidence; third-party rails cannot bypass provider review.
impact: Control domain only: `conclusion: "no-known-incident"` now means no known control-domain incident in the window (key, signer, verifier or admin compromise; unauthorized or unbacked mint, burn or release; theft or escrow drain; stuck or lost supply; unauthorized upgrade, peer or verification-config change; a pause still current at reviewedAt). Operational, peg and wrapper events are enumerated in each surface's finding and sources; a resolved in-window operational incident without integrity failure qualifies with citation, and an unresolved one naming a covered lane removes that lane from coverage.

Provider incident disclosures (OP-IR ruling 2): a provider review carries a required `providerIncidents` array (empty means searched, none found), each disclosure naming its class, exposure interval, compromised verifiers, affected routes, cited sources and any lane-level exemptions. A `verifier-compromise` whose exposure intersects the review window blocks every covered lane that the compromised verifier alone could have satisfied unless the lane proves it was deployed after the exposure or has a pinned point-in-time verification-config read showing the compromised set cannot satisfy the threshold; no observed exploit is not an exemption. Only `verifier-compromise` carries exemptions, and the other classes' affected routes may not be covered lanes.

Derived certificate join (OP-IR ruling 5b): authored reviews name no certificate. The screening set is the digest of the subject lane, the frozen screening policy, the sorted descriptor contributor control ids and the emitter runtime pins, so an added contributor, emitter or pin starts a new chain and inherits nothing. The router joins the newest admitted certificate for `(subjectDeploymentKey, screeningSetId)`, requires `no-material-admin-event`, a contiguous chain and a window end within `laneIncidentCertificateMaxAgeSec` (2,592,000 seconds). The capability gate is deleted: a provider review witnesses the rail, and asset-specific absence is the certificate plus the issuer surface.

Route-level rail authority (OQ-2): `bridgeRouteRisk.routes[]` gains optional `rail: "issuer-operated"` and `providerKeys` from the closed provider vocabulary. On an issuer-operated rail the issuer-surface review is the rail witness and the provider witness list is empty; absent `providerKeys` means no provider-screening closure for that route, never that the route has no provider.

Issuer-surface rows are route-level: `coveredControls` is removed and `asset:<id>` routes are rejected, because contributor completeness is the fact's authored control-id set matched against the descriptor (one authority). Provider rows also drop `coveredControls` and `laneScreeningRefs`. Authored data carrying either removed shape fails the incident-review gate, as does a provider review without its disclosure array or a renewal that drops an incident another current review of the same provider discloses.

Public label: the incident datum's witness label changes from "incident status" to "control incident status", so an open or closed datum never reads as "no incidents at all". The earlier V39-CORE code-only replay measured 103 diagnostic reason/witness-text diffs and no score changes; that historical result is not the integrated local-registry release measurement.

Evidence binds only where a review closed something: provider and issuer-surface evidence attaches to the exact `control:<controlKey>` lanes whose derived coverage names it and is not admitted when it closed none, so evidence is never an orphan witness.

Release scope: only the five reviewed pilot lanes can use certificate closure, after their first post-deploy v2 screening certificates. Earlier v1 certificates cannot close them. Other lanes remain open without reviewed descriptor coverage and all required witnesses. The 2026-10-30 10:17 UTC capture (clock 1793355466) contains no lane certificates, so certificate closure contributes no movers; separately authored incident reviews can still move scores and are measured by the local-registry release gate, not attributed to certificates. Replay captures the exact descriptor and certificate inputs consumed. Version 10.39 activates on the release cut; effectiveAt is provisional and must be re-dated at cut. No deployment or production acceptance is claimed.

title: Evidence-method admission and stable incident identity
summary: Methodology 10.38 admits the evidence methods its scoring code already reads: ERC-4626 clamped executions publish as exact lower bounds, reference-price legs carry a 7,200-second evaluation-lag margin, chain-supply evidence ages against per-source ceilings, and a pinned deployment supply census can bound a deployment's share below 1%, a bound both the documentation class and the Control scorer read. Incident reviews move to authored stable identity; certificate-based lane closure is not part of this release. Weights, thresholds and pillar arithmetic are unchanged.
impact: ERC-4626 lower-bound admission (PF-A1a/PF-A1b). A request above the vault's issued shares keeps the stress units as requestedRawInput, records the clamp in the canonical attempt and emits erc4626-request-exceeds-issued-shares; executableUsd is the served fraction of the ask and the certificate can only be exact-lower-bound, never exact-complete. Admission compares exact units only for exact-complete: a certified lower bound in (0, expected] is admitted and zero is rejected by the certificate schema. A failed totalSupply read stays erc4626-read-unavailable and a simulated zero stays a diagnostic zero, never a clamp-to-zero success. Only an exact-complete same-rail certificate supersedes a modelled route; a lower-bound certificate competes on route score instead, and a shared physical rail is still valued once.

Evaluation-lag margin (PF-A2). Capture withholds a reference-price leg whose age exceeds priceMaxAgeSec minus evaluationLagSec (18,000 minus 7,200 = 10,800 seconds) or that postdates the capture clock, naming the binding leg (execution-price-leg-stale:output|input). The margin is policy-owned and withhold-only: no leg is renewed, re-dated or synthesized, and the evaluator still fails closed on its own price budget. The one measured lag (steakeurcv, 14,265 seconds) therefore leaves those items reasoned-open rather than falsely stale; the first cycle measures the persistent lag and may raise evaluationLagSec, never loosen the window.

Per-source chain-supply ceilings (PF-B3). semantic.supplyAttribution.chainSupplyMaxAgeBySource declares defaultMaxAgeSec 1,800 and carryForwardExtraSec 3,600; report-cards-chain-circulating and deployment-supply-census-v1 are listed at the 5,400-second ceiling. An unlisted source fails closed to the default plus carry, a source's declared window may only tighten that default, and safetyScoreV9ChainSupplySourceId is the single authority for both the published evidence source id and its ceiling.

Deployment supply census admission (SA-3/SA-FIX). The fixed input may carry safetyScoreV9DeploymentSupplyCensusById[assetId] with a packet whose rows are evidenceKind: upper-bound, pinned per chain (EVM header with runtime code hash, finalized Solana slot, or Move ledger version) and conservation-recomputed from its own rows. A generation binding (generationId, registryFingerprint, sourceBaseInputGenerationId) must travel with the map; a map without it is census-rejected:generation-unbound and one built for another registry/base generation is census-rejected:generation-mismatch, both asset-level .pipeline.bridgeJoinDiagnostics.deploymentSupplyCensus outcomes, never an empty census; they publish on the asset's bridge diagnostics whether or not it has a supply review, and an unusable aggregate denominator is census-rejected:read-unavailable rather than a conservation breach. A sub-1% bound is admitted as a reconciled upper bound that both the documentation class and the Control scorer read: the deployment can become non-binding, so census admission can move Control scores once its producer serves packets. A bound at or above 1% yields deployment-supply-share-requires-reviewed-escrow and grants no share. Packet pins and prices stay within 1,800 seconds, while serving and admission now use the declared 5,400-second census ceiling (widened from 1,800 seconds) with no carry-forward. The attribution generation carries the map and binding and the compute path layers them onto the fixed input; both are excluded from the base-input digest, so replay identity does not move.

Stable incident identity (IR-0/1a/1b/1d/2a/2b/5). Negative reviews resolve by their authored identity and scope (asset plus stable reviewId) and are keyed per (assetId, reviewId) at runtime; retired rows keep their original scope and resolve nothing. Provider and issuer-surface rows are parsed, validated and non-closing: laneIncidentCertificateMaxAgeSec is declared policy but no consumer admits a certificate, so coverage data grants no closure in this release. The incident-review key gate rejects missing keys and placeholder certificate refs (coverage-ref-placeholder). Certificate-based lane closure is v10.39 work.

Not claimed: first-cycle Exit movement and separate producer lanes. The Exit producer changes (ERC-4626 clamp, capture price margin) ship in this release's worker. From the first redemption-backstop cycle they can still change Exit capacity and route selection: a clamped route publishes a lower-bound certificate where the stress ask exceeded the vault's issued shares, a leg aged between 10,800 and 18,000 seconds is withheld, and certificate routes compete with same-rail models. A fixed-clock replay cannot measure this because replay consumes captured certificates and runs no producer; the first cycle attributes it, and the v10.38 Exit grade flips against main are 0 pending that re-measure. Census, screening, reserve, supply and peg producers ship separately and are not part of this release: until they serve evidence, the census key is absent from every fixed input and their admissions are inert. No production acceptance or deployment is claimed here; the fixed-clock mover gate is recorded in the release report.

title: Documentation gaps: a score-neutral evidence class
summary: Methodology 10.37 adds a policy-owned documentation class for open questions that cannot materially move a published score. On capture A it classifies 1,447 facts (1,450 datums) behind 915 of 2,877 open questions (934 open, 1,028 issuer, 915 documentation) across six reasons, annotates 23 Economic Control pillars as limited only by documentation gaps, and leaves every score, grade, evidence level, premium, cap, cause and binding byte-identical.
impact: Documentation class: an open cause-C/U compiled gap is documentation-classed at read time by the shared classifier when a policy reason says resolving it cannot move a published score. Six reasons, in policy order: no-scoring-path (custody factorKey keyCustody, which no scored component reads), unknown-scores-as-no-credit (mint reconciliation or supervision already unknown on the Control pillar), unscored-diagnostic (policy defaultTreatment diagnostic; vetoed when the gap is the sole cause of an excluded or null pillar, including any optional-exit route not in the evaluated inventory's admitted routes), coverage-label (incomplete-dex-route-coverage plus a local exit-portfolio-coverage component; never an inventory with zero routes), immaterial-deployment (deployment scope, share = materialSupplyShare ?? the scorer's own proven null-share deployment bound, strictly below documentationImmaterialSharePct 1, and bindingByMateriality false; null share, global scope and reserve claims never qualify) and reserve-dust (collateral-exposure missing rows, exposure weight strictly below reserveDustBookSharePct 0.01 of the book, with the merged per-root residual below reserveDustResidualMaxBookSharePct 0.1). Bars live only in semantic.evidence.documentation; maxAttributableScorePoints stays 0.1.

Capture A (clock 1793294244) documentation datums by reason: immaterial-deployment 677, no-scoring-path 256, coverage-label 162, reserve-dust 160 (157 gaps), unknown-scores-as-no-credit 148, unscored-diagnostic 47; 1,450 datums and 1,447 facts in total. The class is derived, never priced: pricing, cause, responsibility, binding, mixture, caps, gap identity and factSetDigest stay byte-identical, and a mixed C/U question stays issuer/open under documentation > issuer > open precedence.

One evidence level, unchanged (owner decision B). Nothing in the evaluator writes evidenceLevel, limitedEvidenceCauses or limitingCauseGapIds, because those feed the asset-premium gate, the trace's limiting pillars, dependents' propagated cause and the parent Backing inheritance cause. Instead the publication emits openEvidence.byCard[].documentationOnlyLimited, and a card renders "Evidence: limited · documentation gaps only" only under the fail-closed rule: the pillar is limited, its limitingCauseGapIds list is non-empty, and every id resolves locally or through foreignCauseGaps to a documentation gap. One non-documentation witness, an empty list, an unresolved id or any mix leaves the pillar plain limited; annotated pillars still count in the Evidence: limited total. Measured on capture A: 23 annotated cards, all Economic Control, and none of the 20 empty-witness pillars (the plan literals 913/907 and 21 empty witnesses are replaced by measured 915 questions / 1,447 facts and 20 on this capture).

Durable lapse: a custody question whose review passes the scoped-question age budget is retained as stale documentation rather than dropped, gated by the single activation authority semantic.evidence.documentation.retainExpiredScopedQuestions and the no-scoring-path reason. The retained gap keeps its original gap id and reviewedAt, publishes observationState stale and binds the question's own authored review as research evidence, never the clock or publication time. Measured on capture A: 243 custody questions, oldest review 2026-10-01, so the first lapse is 2026-12-30 and nothing is stale at activation; the retained gap keeps cause U / responsibility unresearched, with no invented published-evidence-expired relabel.

Counting and registry: the three published numbers are counted once per question at its root asset by the shared authority, so the documentation bucket is the same set the page, API and dataset publish. The missing-data registry moves to schemaVersion 3 with documentation and issuer bands, reads the shared question-key authority instead of a local mirror, and dedupes supplements against compiled tasks: a supplement is dropped only when every obligation it carries maps to a compiled task, any uncovered obligation keeps it, and rows record causalGapIds, uncoveredCauseGapIds, coverageBasis and supplementalTaskId. Measured on capture A: 5,263 items with 5,263 unique taskIds, 19 supplements, 461 projection supplements removed by the dedupe and 5 kept for an uncovered dependency projection; the admitted-route veto reads the evaluator's included flag, so 5 excluded Exit routes stay open scorable work rather than never-closable documentation. The published registry artifact must be regenerated on a capture bound to this policy.

Zero declared movers, measured not assumed: replaying capture A through the wired publication leaves every card's scoreInput, finalScore, grade, evidenceLevel, limitedEvidenceCauses, limitingCauseGapIds, premium, cap, binding and factSetDigest unchanged, byte-identical on all 393 assets; candidate.resultDigest and evaluatedSet.scoreResultDigest rotate only because they bind the policy and build identity, and the payload grows (documentation carriers, the trace's documentation block and summaries[].documentationFactCount). Capture B and the first accepted publication are separate acceptance obligations and are not claimed here.

Planned activation: 2026-10-30 00:00 UTC (provisional release cut; 1793318400); re-date effectiveAt at release if the cut moves. No fixed-clock replay is claimed for production, and no deployment or production acceptance is claimed.

title: Unrounded reserve composition shares
summary: Live reserve composition now publishes measured shares without one-decimal rounding or remainder repair, so a positive holding below the former display precision stays a finite positive share that Backing and dependency inputs can see.
impact: Reserve adapters: the shared slice helpers default to unrounded precision and sixteen adapters that rounded to 1-12 decimals now publish source-derived shares. Positive holdings that rounded to zero (for example a 0.04% credit slice beside a 99.96% parent) are retained, as are sub-display branches that were previously dropped. Identity grouping, zero filtering, source-total validation and capacity arithmetic are unchanged, and a source total off 100% is retained as a source fact instead of being repaired to 100.

Composition-only raw shares: USD.AI, xDAI and ERC4626 vault composition no longer prequantize raw-amount shares, so a positive balance cannot round to zero; an unrepresentable positive share rejects, and an observed zero stays zero.

Movers: reserve-backed Backing and dependency inputs can change slightly where sub-display positive holdings now appear; pillar weights, materiality and admission rules are unchanged. Mover attribution and the first accepted publication are separate obligations.
No fixed-clock replay is claimed. Activation: 2026-10-28 00:00 UTC (release cut; 1793145600), stacked on 10.35; no deployment or production acceptance is claimed.

title: Asset-local measured-route expiry and bounded DEX capture admission
summary: Expired measured DEX history on a contributing route now quarantines only that asset as a pipeline gap instead of holding every rating, and a valid prepared capture is no longer refused because the live DEX generation advanced inside its evidence budgets.
impact: Measured-route expiry: an asset whose post-hysteresis card relies on, or formerly relied on, expired previously mature high-confidence measured DEX history is quarantined as evaluation-failed (dex-stale: route, generation, original window end, clock, budget) and the cohort recompiled until no new asset is detected. Dependents join the affected census, so the 90% unaffected closure, the 271 rateable floor and the coverage floors still hold the cohort; whole-source DEX staleness or unavailability remains a global hold. Assessment fails closed if a detected asset was not quarantined.

Expiry witnesses: the accepted baseline retains each quarantined asset's expired routes with their original window end and budget, because the null-score stub keeps no route identity. A witness clears only when the same route carries a newer embedded window inside its budget; absent rows and new outer snapshots never clear it. Rollback restores the global hold while keeping the witness-aware detector, so unresolved witnesses still hold.

Bounded DEX capture admission: compute admits a captured DEX generation older than live, before compute and again after enrichment, only while the stablecoins capture is at most 4,500 seconds old and its own DEX evidence at most 14,400 seconds old. Captured rows, generation and freshness remain the evaluated evidence; missing, malformed, ahead or future inputs are refused, and cron metadata records both identities, ages, budgets and the verdict.

Accepted replay captures move to schema v3, retaining the prior accepted baseline the publication was admitted against (null only for a genuine bootstrap) so replay reproduces quarantine; v1/v2 captures stay readable without inferred context. Score arithmetic, grade thresholds, weights and evidence-age limits are unchanged.

No fixed-clock replay is claimed. Activation: 2026-10-28 00:00 UTC (release cut; 1793145600). Equivalence on accepted captures and the first accepted publication remain separate obligations; no deployment or production acceptance is claimed.

title: Reserve evidence admission calibration
summary: Live reserve evidence that Backing admits changes in three ways: a reviewed report stays admissible while a newer unreviewed report awaits review, dated-source age budgets follow each publisher's measured cadence, and several reserve adapters now distinguish structural or scheduled source states from real evidence failures.
impact: Newer unreviewed reports: independent-assurance and issuer-report feeds no longer error when the official index lists a report newer than the reviewed pin. The pinned report keeps publishing with a degraded newer-unreviewed-report warning that is scoring-neutral (SCORING_NEUTRAL_DEGRADED_WARNING_CODES); stale-source-data is never excusable. Previously the error left the prior clean snapshot admissible only until the 48-hour fetch budget expired, so a pinned report now stays admissible until its own source-age cap instead.

Source-age budgets: a 150-day lagged-quarterly tier covers attestation-pdf-index and EUROP (Ripio quarterly reports land up to 54 days after quarter end; Schuman successors land at 99-114 days), with per-coin tightening to 70 days for USDU and ZARsc and 46.3 days for ZARP; CADD moves to the 70-day next-month tier; mRE7 14 days, mHYPER and mMEV 9 days from measured oracle round gaps.

Adapter semantics feeding Backing: Matrixdock XAGm degrades on feed age only when reserve/supply divergence exceeds 0.05%; Mento FX-market closure is informational; Bridge degrades on itemized-backing shortfall or components above published reserves rather than an unitemized surplus; OnRe degrades only when the holdings schedule falls below NAV; EVM branch coverage uses the shared 0.995 shortfall threshold; USD0 publishes self-referential claims as very-high-risk slices and withholds its ratio while they are material; sUSDai and USDD gain on-chain or history-joined corroboration paths. Curated changes (XAUm curated single gold slice, FIUSD native-fund-share scope, usdx-axis venue mapping, fxSAVE queue-redeem route) are curation, recorded here for attribution.

No fixed-clock replay is claimed. Planned activation is provisionally 2026-10-25 00:00 UTC (1792886400); re-date effectiveAt at release. Equivalence on accepted captures and the first accepted publication remain separate obligations; no deployment or production acceptance is claimed.

title: Reviewed finality margins for supply-attribution pins
summary: Reviewed economic supply partitions whose deployments include a chain with a reviewed finalized-head lag margin get one widened pin window: the 1800s observation age limit plus the largest margin among the asset's chains. Rollup finalized heads trail Ethereum's, so the coherent pin set of an Arbitrum, Base, Optimism or MegaETH partition was rejected by construction near the 1800s limit.
impact: Policy: supplyAttribution.finalityMarginSecByChainId sets Arbitrum 600s, Base 600s, Optimism 900s and MegaETH 1500s; every other chain has no margin. The effective pin window of a reviewed economic partition is observationMaxAgeSec plus the largest margin among its deployment chains, added once per asset because alignment ages every pin in the set to the oldest one. A margin cannot exceed the base window.

The same window binds capture pin admission (finalized-head freshness, the reserved capture-window check, recent-pin RPC routing), the CCIP, LayerZero OFT, Curve and canonical-messenger pending observers, final capture ageing, partition derivation (deployment-observation-current) and Score's chain-supply evidence budget for the accepted packet. Aggregate, reference-price and conversion budgets, the 120s skew limit, finality requirements, canonical hashes and full conservation are unchanged.

Evidence: finalized-head lag sampled every ~20s for 30 minutes on 2026-10-23 was Ethereum 770-1152s, Arbitrum 826-1273s, Base 913-1536s, Optimism 894-1646s and MegaETH 1755-2165s; the largest same-instant excess over Ethereum was 423s, 424s, 828s and 1375s. Each margin is that excess rounded up to the next 300s, which leaves each rollup at least the capture headroom Ethereum-only partitions already have. In production, sdola-inverse-finance's anchors were rejected with capture-freshness-window-insufficient (Arbitrum and Ethereum anchors aligned to the oldest rollup pin) in four of its 2026-10-23 journal attempts, and witry-brix failed every run at pinning because its MegaETH finalized pin (about 2010s old) exceeded 1800s. MegaETH keeps finalized pins because its witry OFT escrow source requires finality; the margin is used instead of redesigning OFT checkpoint semantics around safe-lag pins.

sdola-inverse-finance also fails on asset-timeout, CCIP history-incomplete and its Base route in other runs; this release addresses only the pin-age rejection. No fixed-clock replay is claimed. Replays of accepted captures can differ only where an accepted packet on a margin chain aged past 1800s by the scoring clock; new movers follow only from newly admitted packets. Activation: 2026-10-23 00:00 UTC (release cut; 1792713600), shared with v10.32; v10.33 is the version at that cut. Equivalence on accepted captures, the first accepted publication and attribution acceptance remain separate obligations; no deployment or production acceptance is claimed.

title: Hourly publication cadence
summary: Safety Score v10.32 publishes once an hour at :22 instead of every 30 minutes; budgets defined as multiples of the publication or preparation cadence scale with it, while score arithmetic, grade thresholds, pillar weights and evidence-age policy constants are unchanged.
impact: Cadence — compute-safety-score-v9 runs hourly at :22 and its fixed input is prepared hourly on the :16 DEX publication tick; the :46 tick prepares only after publishing a late DEX stage.

Derived bounds — the accepted-publication freshness bound (2 × the publication cadence) moves from 3,600 to 7,200 seconds. It governs endpoint staleness (X-Safety-Score-Freshness-Budget), consumer fail-close, and the evaluator's lenderCollateralBacking freshness, so previous accepted collateral scores are admitted for up to two hours. A capture lagging the live stablecoins cache is admitted for one missed hourly prepare (4,500 s instead of 2,700 s), and the supply-attribution source input for one preparation cycle (3,600 s instead of 1,800 s). Scores still use the capture's frozen clock.

Unchanged — supply-attribution observation age (1,800 s) and its 10.26 carry-forward (+1,800 s) keep their values; the carry-forward is now shorter than one hourly cycle, so a missed attribution run reaches the unavailable-materiality fallback one cycle sooner. DEX, measured-history, live-reserve and chain-supply windows are unchanged.
Effect — scores can differ from v10.31 only where an input is admitted under the longer lender-collateral bound or a lagging capture; no replay or mover census is claimed.
Released 2026-10-23 (effectiveAt 1792713600) after slot catch-up and cadence-scaled status grading were live.

title: Exposure-weighted local authority
summary: Safety Score v10.31 prices known-share deployment-local authority through a resolved mixture of the same aggregation and peg pipeline used for global Control. There is no materiality threshold; the Control pillar retains global paths, while local authority is disclosed in deployment adjustments.
impact: Methodology — preCap = R(B) − Σ s_i × (R(B) − R(B_q_i)). B uses priced-unknown aggregation pillars and the peg multiplier; B_q replaces resolved Control C with min(C, q). Neither endpoint includes caps, rounding or the USDT premium. R resolves non-authority deployment signals only.

Authority class — all graded deployment-local mint/admin/upgrade components, including bounded and partially bounded powers and active incidents on those controls. Group by deployment/liability slice and take its worst quality. Every known-share local authority is non-binding; null-share controls keep fail-closed binding. Bridge mint components and bridge incidents remain infrastructure, with bridge-tier pricing retained; oracle behavior is unchanged.

Allocation — authority slices are disjoint liabilities, not normalization weights. Retain every own share without trimming or rescaling, at every total: loss = min(worst global-equivalent loss, sum of share-weighted counterfactual losses). Totals through 1.001 are tolerated rounding noise; larger totals emit an explicit overlap diagnostic.

Attribution — dominated authority paths cost zero naturally, while worse local powers remain priced even under a shared root. Exact mint/upgrade common-mode controller rows owned by the local-authority lane are diagnostic, not a second charge; independent bridge, oracle and chain infrastructure remains priced. Fully supported local-only inventories use neutral pre-authority Control90; genuine gaps keep their handling. Authority ownership survives serialized score-input round trips. Authority rows follow infrastructure rows with resolved counterfactual exposed scores; infrastructure allocations may change as authority leaves their normalization pool.

Activation evidence — fixed-clock engine replays of two production captures (2026-10-22T17:19Z and 19:18Z, 395 assets each, zero quarantines) against v10.30 give identical movers: 10 score movers, all up, 7 rated-grade upgrades, 0 downgrades. fxUSD C+60→B−68, DOC C+60→B−68, sUSDC-v1 C+60→B−65, spUSDT C+60→B−65, eUSD C+63→B−65, fxSAVE C−50→C58 (through its fxUSD parent), vCHF C55→C58, eEarn C−53→C56 (a bounded local minter no longer binds Control; Control 50→60), BTCUSD D46→D48 and USDCV A−80→A−81; no production acceptance is claimed. Material bounded local powers that previously bound Control now use exposure-weighted pricing. Existing two-publication grade hysteresis may hold a prior letter on the first accepted publication; review gradeHold and provisional labels alongside scores, dependencies and the post-deploy first-cycle check.

Mover disclosure — listed score/grade movers are post-cap outcomes, not a complete pre-cap movement census. Both captures also show cap-masked pre-cap changes: musd −0.36; usdat 62.47→66.29 masked at 62, with its parent cap becoming binding; syusd +0.67 and usdnr +0.013. Capped children can change pre-cap stages or cap binding without changing their published score or letter.

Public explanation — optional local-admin exposure shows the weakest priced local quality, full covered supply share and up to three deployments by modeled loss under the unchanged Control pillar on the stablecoin page only; the Safety Scores grid and compare radar omit it. This display is priced in the score, not a score-equivalent Control number; scores, grades and methodology version are unchanged. Readers ship before emission.
Activation: 2026-10-22 20:00 UTC (release cut; 1792699200). Production acceptance follows the first accepted publications.

title: Active-depeg severity ladder and exact-certificate Exit confidence
summary: Safety Score v10.30 deepens the uniform active-depeg severity ladder and raises model confidence only for admitted exact execution certificates. It also records dated vault-pricing, reserve and wrapper-assurance corrections, the score-neutral BD-basedollar refresh, VCRED delisting, partial-evidence display improvements and a tooling-only worklist fix. Observation confidence, execution admission and measurement rules, non-certificate models and other scoring rules remain unchanged; fixed-clock replay is not production acceptance.
impact: Methodology — active depegs at least 10% retain the score limit of 49 (D); at least 25% now limits the score to 25 and at least 50% limits it to 10, both within the F range. Select severity from the maximum absolute peak among open events, not current spot deviation or closed events. In the fixed-clock replay, msUSD moves 25→10, USDA-avalon 39→25 and USDX-kava 39→25; pmUSD is capped at 10 (18→10).

Methodology — raise medium model confidence for admitted exact on-chain same-notional redemption execution certificates from 0.75 to 0.85; observation confidence stays 0.85. Preserve exact identity, original clocks, request/cost/output admission, measured capacity, completion, settlement and queue limitations. Non-certificate model confidence is unchanged. Fixed-clock replay examples include yBOLD 70→72, yvUSDC 65→68 and gtUSDC 66→69; these are replayed effects, not production acceptance.
Tracking — VCRED is delisted from tracking: no admissible price source since 2026-09-07 and no reserve evidence; not a death/cemetery entry.

Evidence refresh — BD-basedollar mint authority is refreshed for its sourced SaferSafes timelock and effective authority paths; this is a factual evidence update, not asset-specific methodology or renewed older review dates. The refresh is score-neutral because Control remains 60, bound by the token-contract row.

Public explanation — radar/partial-evidence display distinguishes unassessed or excluded pillars from assessed risk, preserving partial-evidence provenance without inventing numeric axes or changing scores.

Vault research — the 2026-10-22 review establishes privileged internal pricing for strategy/NAV vault share pricing at syrupUSDT, hbUSDT and DUSD (Control 60→45). spUSDT's chi/VSR accumulator is a savings-rate setter under the existing rule; its oracle profile does not price. Reserve envelopes were refreshed for Saturn sUSDat, sYUSD, Umbrella stkGHO, Yearn USDC and Noble USDN, with open-ended maturity facts for sYUSD and stkGHO. Exit research found no admissible new execution models.

Assurance correction — unsupported parent-only reconciliation/supervision credits were withdrawn from 12 wrapper admin reviews: apyUSD, ctUSD, cUSDO, iUSD, mUSD, pUSD, sUSN, sYUSD, USDN, USDnr, USDSC and wM. spUSDT's inherited Tether credits were also withdrawn (Control 90→65, score 64→60, still C+). Original review clocks are retained; the corrections are dated 2026-10-22.
Worklist fix — The missing-data worklist routes all mechanism-review components; this is tooling only, with no score effect.

title: Bounded carry-forward of retained per-asset circulating supply
summary: When the stablecoin supply sync has not re-observed an asset, its last observed per-asset circulating supply stays usable for a bounded, named window beyond the chain-supply budget, so Exit can size its stress request instead of dropping to its fallback floor for one run.
impact: Chain-supply carry-forward: for an asset without a supply-attribution packet whose per-asset supply observation (retained by sync-stablecoins with its original supplyObservedAt) is older than the 1800s chain-supply budget, the budget widens by four sync-stablecoins intervals to 5400s. The chain-supply evidence keeps the original observation clock and chain-supply generation and names the widened budget and age. A fresh observation always replaces the retained one, so the window cannot mask a supply move the provider reports; observations past 5400s, assets without a per-asset observation clock, and attributed or economic partitions keep their existing treatment.

Before 10.27 a retained observation past 1800s made the supply fact stale, Exit could not size its stress request and fell to the bounded floor with missing-same-notional-route. A real collapse still trips the depeg and DEWS signals, and a reader-level fix (a validated zero becomes unavailable instead of restored) is a separate owner decision.

title: Bounded carry-forward of runtime inputs and grade hysteresis
summary: A redemption disclosure admitted by its run and the last admitted wM/XAUT deployment supply attribution are carried forward for a bounded, named window instead of dropping Exit or Control to their fallback for one run, and a published letter grade changes only after two consecutive publications compute the same new band.
impact: Grade hysteresis: when a rated card's computed band differs from both its previously published grade and the band of the previous publication's raw score, the card keeps the previously published grade and discloses gradeHold { rawGrade, heldFromGenerationId }. The numeric score, pillars, caps and dependency inputs stay raw and unclamped; children consume parent scores, never held grades. Rating-status transitions (NR, pipeline-gap) and cards without an accepted rated baseline are never held. Causal D/F proof requirements follow the raw band.

Redemption route carry-forward: a verified-source live-reserve disclosure admitted as source- and fetch-fresh by a redemption run is carried forward until that run's own budget (two producer intervals: the next scheduled refresh plus one retry) expires, keeping its original observation clock, the redemption generation and the effective budget. The same bounded rule applies to capture-time consumed-reserve admission, which previously withheld the redemption row with redemption-reserve-input-stale; carried rows are reported with their reserve generation, assessment clock, age and carry deadline. A run that assesses the disclosure as stale never admits or renews it. This removes the iUSD sawtooth in which a 6-hour source budget measured from a disclosure about 2 hours older than its fetch lapsed minutes before the next 4-hourly run, dropping Exit to its fallback for one publication.

Supply-attribution carry-forward: when a run's supply-attribution generation rejects, omits or ages out an expected reviewed-deployment (wM) or lock/mint (XAUT) packet, the last admitted packet is re-derived against the current aggregate supply and admitted for one further 30-minute consumer cycle beyond its own observation bound (wM 1800s to 3600s, XAUT 3600s to 5400s). The packet keeps its original observation clocks, names carriedForwardFromGenerationId, and its chain-supply evidence names the widened budget; compute metadata lists carriedForwardAssetIds. Beyond the window the existing unavailable-materiality fallback applies. Economic-partition packets are not carried.

Journal replay (2026-10-13 to 2026-10-21, accepted publications expanded per publication, same evaluation build, reason-code proxies): 956 raw letter-grade changes; redemption carry-forward alone leaves about 927, plus supply-attribution carry-forward about 810, plus hysteresis about 524. The largest remaining classes are continuous measured inputs (DEX depth near a band edge) and Exit stress-request sizing when an asset's circulating supply is unavailable or stale in a run (sYUSD, yBOLD, USDnr, USDsc), which is not carried forward in this release.

Pillar weights, grade bands, caps, evidence freshness budgets other than the bounded carry-forward windows, and fail-closed publication holds are unchanged. Planned activation is provisionally 2026-10-22 00:00 UTC (1792627200), following the next-UTC-midnight convention; re-date effectiveAt at release. Two-capture equivalence, the first accepted production publication and post-deploy grade-stability observation remain separate acceptance obligations; no deployment or production acceptance is claimed.

title: V10: curation, owner rulings, and physical-to-USD Exit
summary: V10 is a major release consolidating the 2026-10-01 curation pass, owner rulings, and physical-to-USD Exit. It brings known-supply Exit sizing, whole-book custody and report-date discipline, measured collateralization, deployment-local control pricing, adverse mint evidence continuity, wrapper and inheritance corrections, and reviewed physical-metal redemption composed with conservative USD sales. Missing evidence never grants credit.
impact: The Exit-only supply projection admits a bounded-unknown supply fact only when its required policy rule is v9.supply.bridge-materiality, the producer's marker that the current amount is established but its partition is not. Known supply keeps its existing behavior, and the reviewed stress fraction, grid, cost bound, and settlement horizon are unchanged.

Missing bridge profiles, ambiguous route joins, and missing or rejected attribution packets no longer suppress Exit sizing when a current circulating amount is established. No bridge shares, chain distribution, transfer materiality, control facts, or evidence gaps are inferred or promoted; their existing gaps and ceilings remain.

Sizing is not executable-capacity evidence: every route still needs the existing same-notional capacity, output valuation, cost, access, and settlement admission. Exit and downstream scores may change where measured routes can now be compared, without guaranteeing a grade improvement.

Asset-wide institutional custody labels now require whole-book evidence. Custody gains mixed and unknown values; omitted custody for centralized or RWA-backed classes defaults to unknown instead of an institutional label, while structural on-chain defaults remain. Mixed and unknown never qualify for regulated-only or on-chain-only Selector eligibility and add no numeric Safety Score credit.

Explicitly adapter-owned reserve compositions keep their own date when a separately evidenced monthly report has a known period end and publication date. Curated-only compositions keep report-period lockstep, audit-grade admission still requires matching periods, and independently dated fallback rows retain only their own static-validated evidence, completeness, and freshness gates.

Dated, primary-source-backed catalog withholding replaces sUSD1+'s hardcoded parent Backing exception without removing its parent cap or peg relationship. Privileged wrapper-local NAV pricing remains high risk without a whole-score ceiling; direct-wrapper onchain custody relief requires current fully-onchain allocation proof or complete zero-unknown-exposure custody checks.

Security history gains an informational record for disclosed, remediated, non-realized vulnerabilities (USD3 batch auction, XAUT transferFrom, fxUSD router), dated from primary disclosures, with no realized-exploit, loss, or mint-incident routing.

Mint-control selection prices the worst applicable durable-mint authority across deployments: native root issuance stays asset-wide, and proved deployment-local controls keep supply-weighted treatment.

Privileged-pricing ceilings are removed while the oracle Control component retains its 45-point bound. Evidence-backed adverse mint findings survive unresolved reviews until positive evidence clears them.

A reserve report without an explicit publication date may use its exact printed signed or as-of date as a typed, visibly signed conservative publication stand-in. Chronology, report age, composition lockstep, and assurance-scope gates remain; no later date is invented.

Adverse minority mint authorities remain published and proportionally charged by deployment exposure; expired aggregate reviews preserve each control's own adverse or unknown evidence. Unresolved pricing charges the full admitted unresolved/unknown/unreviewed cohort, proportionally below 5%, smoothly blending the whole-coin ceiling from 5–15%, and fully at 15% or unknown shares, with interpolated cap traces and aggregate-aware bridge joins.

Measured collateralization retains source, dated evidence and stable measurement identity. Ratios below 100% cap Backing, including inherited reserve quality, only with current evidence within the mechanism-overlay freshness budget; expired, undated or unevidenced measurements grant neither haircut nor credit. Serial wrappers apply the same inherited parent measurement once, while distinct local shortfalls remain chargeable.

Reviewed physical-metal redemption composes with conservative modelled USD sales under the 500-bps admission ceiling, lot arithmetic, expiry and captured-price gates; execution cost uses the common request denominator and public traces prevent double counting. Modelled capacity is bounded by evidenced throughput over the complete settlement window or one minimum lot; verified customers receive no institutional discount, coverage is explicitly modelled, fee and timing assumptions lower confidence, and best-effort cash branches retain the policy sale spread.

Reviewed physical-to-USD terms cover ten commodity assets, preserving conservative delivery scope, lot identity, published fees, and settlement gaps. Physical delivery alone remains diagnostic rather than USD Exit credit.

Oracle applicability follows exact reviewed issuance paths: evidenced non-price-sensitive GHO allocations emit no scored component without hiding lending gaps, and Horizon's externally relayed NAV tier is admitted under its documented-feed-heartbeat owner ruling without implying enforced timestamp rejection.

Risk-absorption wrappers retain local emergency and slashing/configuration loss controls without parent first-loss credit. Parent-only custody uncertainty leaves local strategy complexity only when current reviewed allocation and reserve facts establish a direct single-parent claim; expired proof and local private-credit exposure remain conservative.

Fresh, uniquely keyed classification-only reserve reviews supply classification metadata without certifying whole-book composition, changing unknown exposure, replacing live percentages, restoring withheld pooled dependency weights or overriding non-link dispositions.

BabelFish and USD0 branch-reserve censuses are corrected and USD0 registry drift is guarded. Census and valuation remain separate: unavailable exposure stays unknown, and USD0-denominated self-referential claims stay unclassified pending reviewed netting and an independent-backing denominator.

Reviewed economic-deployment attribution preserves the original circulating aggregate and source generations, using exhaustive exact holding censuses, independently timed conversions, primary-proven escrow/receipt/exclusion/in-flight reconciliation and hash-bound EVM, Solana and XRPL observations. Partial-provider renormalization is rejected; exact native/wrapper deployment keys govern transfer materiality. Existing native-single-route and independent-lane eligibility moves into reviewed registry data without new coin allocations; unresolved-control bands and issuer non-disclosure charges remain.

Local exact-request Exit certificates add integer-unit order-book and off-ramp execution, policy admission, independent compiler/evaluator verification and sanitized public proof traces. Reviewed identities remain empty; existing scored routes, canonical supply, pool census and documented issuer charges are unchanged.

Deployment-bound, execution-complete control scope covers latent, re-enabled and counterfactual paths and Safe-extension noninterference without absence credit. Weighted contract and XRPL signing uses minimum cryptographic signatures, including master/RegularKey bypasses, without human-independence credit. Unreviewed or stale siblings retain uncertainty/adverse treatment, and native bridge-mint/burn rails remain controlled.
XRPL issued amounts retain exact decimal-string coefficient/exponent semantics instead of fabricated fixed decimals; fixed-unit readers reject native XRPL.

Exact-contract and independently dated per-dimension allocation evidence retains conservative entity/holder completeness and worst-risk aggregation. Scoped claims cannot satisfy whole-allocation/A3 proof; parent legal context is adverse-only, while issuer non-disclosure charges, adverse facts, supply accounting and parent caps remain.

New capabilities activate only on their own reviewed data; without new reviewed data the production capture replays identically. Partial execution scopes and weighted quorums cannot worsen legacy Control unless they add newly verified adverse reach; only closure-complete scope may narrow.

The verified data wave authors native-family identities and overlays for EURSAFO's UCITS/TRS mechanism, Mento shared reserves and USDB/USDU protocol positions; Mento single-relayer oracle profiles; lossless XRPL issued-currency encodings; partial execution scopes; and wrapper scoped claims. Unverified facts remain unresolved and retain their charges.

Scoped financial reports admit exact deployment/book denominators and exclusions, with current-generation liability weighting and charged unknown residuals. Without an admitted current partition and book join, exact coverage remains diagnostic and preserves legacy report treatment; only verified exclusions of nonzero or unknown-amount still-owed liabilities may remove overbroad credit.

Independently dated standing feeder identity and header-bound on-chain observations use separate admission lanes, including reviewed reserve/escrow contracts and native technical subjects. They never grant financial assurance, supply or current-holdings credit.

Bounded reserve facts distinguish contractual maturity maxima, observed tenor, exhaustive enforceable eligibility, current native availability, structural applicability and stressed final realization. Exact current scope, coverage and freshness are required; undisclosed composition, concentration, unknown tails and original constraints remain charged. Origin's same-pin idle USDC fraction adds no redemption capacity; its cross-chain observation remains diagnostic pending reconciliation.

Reviewed receipt/bridge reserve-access graphs retain originating authorities and exact deployments, deduplicate physical positions and expose unpriced or unresolved remainder. Public freeze look-through is diagnostic-only, independent of holder-transfer posture, with no new freeze penalty or economic score change.

Verified data wave B adds scoped reports for USDtb, QCAD and VCHF; bounded observations for xDAI and LVUSD; HLSCOPE standing feeder identity; CASH, STAC and OUSD maturity/liquidity facts; and Nexus NUSD, NXUSD, yzUSD and syzUSD access graphs. Unjoined scopes remain monotonic and diagnostic.

Positively proven, runtime-bound Safe-module reach is recognised even in a partial control inventory, exposing verified adverse paths such as OUSD's signature-free vault withdrawals; only exhaustive closure grants a noninterference waiver, and partial inventories still add no charge for unsearched closure.

Verified data wave C resolves unknowns that had lowered scores: Zilliqa is registered so XSGD's issuer-native deployment joins its reviewed controls; frxUSD satellite deployments, stkGHO role holders, yzUSD collateral-funded minting, USDU internal pricing, sUSDD/sDOLA on-chain custody, scrvUSD satellites and OUSD's Safe modules are authored from pinned reads. Disclosed issuer internal mint-ledger reconciliation (Quantoz EURQ and USDQ) resolves only the issuer-backend Control process question, without cadence, financial-assurance or key-custody credit; independent reserve assurance stays charged in Backing.

Centrifuge deployment attribution keeps reviewed sibling deployments when an unresolved route has positively observed zero raw supply in the same generation; nonzero or unobserved unresolved routes still reject, and the unresolved route's controls stay charged.

A fresh reviewer-scoped question on an admitted partial mint scope whose active path has unknown reach keeps that controller bounded-unknown under the existing limited-evidence treatment instead of compiling it as known global-claim reach with inferred incident absence. A separately reviewed path that establishes global, unbounded mint power keeps its adverse posture and structural failure.

A Not-Rated wave researched all 18 unrated coins with independent verification. Ratings come only from verified facts; coins that remain Not Rated keep their documented research and unknown-is-not-zero charges.

Complete, verified, dated curated compositions and whole-asset portfolio observations admit an explicitly reconciled unclassified residual at or below the policy-owned 0.1% floor. The residual stays charged as bounded-unknown; above-threshold, unrecorded or unchargeably small positive tails reject, and zero-residual behavior is unchanged.

Reviewed, dated, primary-sourced suspension removes only an exact redemption channel's capacity and credit, with public diagnostics. Independent routes retain their evidence; suspension cannot infer total-exit failure, measured-adverse attribution, lifecycle or wind-down. VNXAU's legacy vnx.li rail is suspended without rating the asset.

Inventoried deployments with unresolved economic boundaries use the smooth supply-share band without a second Control evidence cliff below 15%. Observed zero and captured shares retain bounded facts and gaps; unknown shares, exposure at or above 15%, out-of-cohort uncertainty and verified adverse charges retain their treatment.

All six reviewed registries isolate malformed asset-local evidence and duplicate keys into precise admission quarantines without blocking healthy assets. Envelope failures remain global; valid-file provenance digests and scoring stay unchanged.

Reviewed finalized EVM pending-message observations supplement HTTPS sources with exhaustive identities and generation-bound block/hash anchors. Unavailable reads and escrow surplus reject; conservation includes excluded receipt holdings. scrvUSD remains unresolved without every satellite's authenticated pending source.

Reviewed, fail-closed provider-row exclusions remove proven distinct liabilities only from unresolved-deployment and unmatched/unreviewed bridge-share numerators, with public proof traces. The original aggregate denominator, provider observations, reconciliation and all other materiality facts remain unchanged.

The decision wave rates mTBILL C-/50 using its verified October 1 composition with a charged 0.0049% residual, and moves FRAX from 55 to 56 by excluding the migrated Fraxtal frxUSD row. AUDM refreshes to September 30, EURQ to August 30 with its 1% residual charged, and ZARP's publication date corrects to September 21; assets without newer reports receive no date bumps.

Exit exhaustion requires score-eligible, output-resolved exact-complete measurements, known or stale. Lower bounds retain positive credit but, like documented terms and modelled capacity, cannot prove exhaustion; non-exhaustive gaps retain bounded uncertainty.

Wrapper unwinds require exact-complete measurements, inherited parent controls are not double-charged, and producer-side gaps do not trigger the missing-facts form fallback. Disclosed unquantified fee formulas retain uncertainty but never score worse than undisclosed fees.

Partial disabled-final execution labels cannot remove established issuance economics: known liability reach and adverse semantics persist until current execution-complete closure proves removal. Unknown activation or reach cannot establish adverse promotion.

Whole-composition obligation closure gates standing and portfolio reserve observations, not partial on-chain technical evidence. Technical observations retain source bindings and unresolved obligations without composition or financial-assurance credit.

Economic accounting rejects overlapping deductions and mixed snapshot tuples, reconciles canonical provider aliases, isolates malformed plans per asset and requires exact-context-slot Solana blocks.
